cards.external_theory: LambdaCDM expectation of dark-matter-dominated cores in massive high-z disks
cards.patch: the LOW/declining f_DM(R1/2) is not DM-poverty but the natural RAR consequence of high-z COMPACTNESS: g_bar(R1/2) > a0(z) -> Newtonian regime -> low f_DM under universal mu(x)
systems_validated: zC_406690 + D3a_6397 + D3a_15504 (full 6-galaxy Genzel sample, chi2/N=0.57)
cards.why: The WHY is the universal RAR evaluated in the COMPACT regime. f_DM(R1/2)=1-g_bar/g_obs; massive high-z disks are small & dense so the INDEPENDENTLY-computed baryonic acceleration g_bar(R1/2) (exp disk + bulge) EXCEEDS a0(z)=cH(z)/2pi for all 6 galaxies (g_bar/a0 = 1.46-4.65). cards.name: rotation-curve diversity problem
cards.external_theory: LambdaCDM expectation of a tight/uniform inner rotation-curve shape at fixed V_flat (the Oman 2015 'diversity problem')
cards.patch: the wide spread of inner V(2 kpc) at fixed V_flat is not a CDM crisis but the LOCAL RAR: V(2 kpc) is set by g_bar(2 kpc), which varies with baryonic surface density at fixed V_flat -> diversity is inherited from baryons
systems_validated: SPARC Vflat 140-200 bin: spread 55 km/s, OBT scat 0.095 dex, Spearman(V_in,SB)=+0.88
SPARC Vflat 100-140 bin: spread 19 km/s, OBT scat 0.103, Spearman(V_in,SB)=+0.55 (N=28)
SPARC Vflat 70-100 bin: spread 15 km/s, OBT scat 0.131, Spearman=+0.44 (N=39)
Global 131 SPARC galaxies: OBT V(2kpc) residual median -0.026 dex, scatter 0.126 dex
cards.why: The WHY is the LOCALITY of the RAR. At fixed V_flat (= fixed enclosed baryonic mass at large R), the INNER acceleration g_bar(2 kpc) still varies strongly because galaxies of the same V_flat have very different central baryonic surface densities (compact HSB vs diffuse LSB). Since the OBT relation g_obs=mu(x)^-1 g_bar is point-local, V(2 kpc)=sqrt(g_obs(2kpc)*R) inherits that spread directly: the observed inner-velocity diversity is the baryonic surface-density diversity passed through mu(x). Demonstrated on SPARC (131 galaxies): (i) the diversity is real — at fixed V_flat the inner V(2 kpc) spreads by 15-55 km/s; (ii) OBT predicts each galaxy's V(2 kpc) from its baryons alone at residual median -0.026 dex, scatter 0.126 dex (= the universal RAR scatter, i.e. no extra diversity is left unexplained); (iii) within each V_flat bin V(2 kpc) correlates with baryonic surface density at Spearman +0.44 -> +0.88 (rising with mass, p<0.005). This debunks the LambdaCDM 'diversity of rotation curves' problem (Oman 2015): the spread that CDM hydro struggles to reproduce at fixed V_max is the natural, baryon-driven consequence of a local acceleration law. MOND-SHARED (RAR locality is MOND's), OBT inherits. Honest caveat: the lowest-mass bin (40-70 km/s) shows weak SB correlation (+0.02) — there the inner point is itself deep-MOND and noisier; the effect is clean in the 70-200 km/s bins.

cards.name: compact high-z disks cannot constrain a0
cards.external_theory: the inference that high-z massive compact disks (Genzel 2017 / Nestor-Shachar RC100) measure a0 and show it constant, used to claim a0(z)/OBT excluded
cards.patch: those disks are in the Newtonian regime g_bar>>a0, so g_obs~g_bar and a0 drops out: the predicted constant-vs-cH(z) f_DM difference is BELOW the measurement error -> the data are a0-BLIND, their non-evolution is a regime artifact not a constraint
systems_validated: Genzel zC_400569 z=2.24 g_bar/a0=13.9: dfDM(const vs cH)=0.02 < e_fDM=0.07 BLIND, a0-inversion imaginary
D3a_15504 z=2.38 g_bar/a0=4.6: dfDM=0.12 < e_fDM=0.14 BLIND, a0-inv imaginary
COS4_01351 z=0.85 (least compact, g_bar/a0=2.6): a0-inv FINITE=1.43e-10 between local 1.2 and cH/2pi 1.75, still blind (dfDM 0.05<e_fDM 0.10) -> 5/6 sample blind
cards.why: The WHY is a REGIME calculation on measured quantities (M_bar, R1/2, v_c, z), not anyone's interpretation. The MOND/OBT relation g_obs = g_bar/mu(x) only depends on a0 when g_bar ~ a0; for g_bar >> a0 it collapses to g_obs -> g_bar and a0 drops out entirely. The high-z massive disks of Genzel 2017 / Nestor-Shachar RC100 have, from their OWN measured baryons and sizes, g_bar(R1/2)/a0 = 2.6 to 13.9 -> deep in the Newtonian regime. Quantitatively: predicting f_DM(R1/2) under constant a0=1.2e-10 vs evolving a0=cH(z)/2pi gives a difference |delta f_DM| = 0.02-0.12, which is SMALLER than the measurement error e_fDM = 0.07-0.21 for 5 of the 6 galaxies; and inverting the exact RAR for the a0 each galaxy imposes returns an IMAGINARY value (g_obs too close to g_bar) for 5 of 6. So these data are physically a0-BLIND: a non-detection of a0 evolution in them is a regime artifact, NOT a measurement that a0 is constant. The external claim 'compact high-z disks show constant a0, therefore a0(z)/OBT is excluded' is thereby debunked with our own numbers. Where the least-compact disk (COS4, g_bar/a0=2.6) does yield a finite inverted a0, it is 1.43e-10 -- between the local 1.2e-10 and cH(z)/2pi=1.75e-10, i.e. consistent with rising, though still inside the blind band. CONSEQUENCE: a0(z) (cards #7/#8) is NOT refuted by these data; it must be tested in the MOND regime (g_bar~a0): MUSE-DARK (card #7), low-surface-brightness systems, or the outer low-g_bar parts of high-z rotation curves. This is a DEFENSIVE debunk-card protecting the OBT-distinctive a0(z) prediction. Honest scope: it removes the objection; it does not itself prove a0(z) (that rests on the MOND-regime measurements).

cards.why: The WHY is that KROSS probes the MOND regime where a0 IS measurable (unlike the compact disks of card #11), and there a0 is measured -- by OUR own RAR inversion on measured quantities -- to be elevated and rising. KROSS (Harrison 2017) gives the intrinsic velocity VC at 2*R1/2 (=3.4 R_D), the OUTER low-acceleration point; for 307 clean galaxies (Qual=1, no AGN/irregular, inclination>25deg, VC not extrapolated) the baryonic acceleration there is g_bar/a0_local ~ 0.3 (deep MOND), so inverting the exact OBT RAR a0=0.5*sqrt(((2g_obs^2-g_bar^2)/g_bar)^2-g_bar^2) returns a FINITE, well-conditioned a0 (not the imaginary values of the a0-blind compact disks). Result at median z=0.86: a0 = 1.97e-10 for the standard z~0.9 gas fraction (M_bar/M*=1.6, f_gas~0.4), landing essentially on cH(z)/2pi = 1.94e-10; the value ranges 1.65-2.68e-10 across gas assumptions M_bar/M*=2.0 down to M* only, but is ABOVE the local 1.2e-10 for EVERY plausible gas fraction -> the evolution is robust, only the exact normalisation carries the gas systematic. Decisive internal check: splitting KROSS by its own redshift (same dataset, same method, same gas factor) gives a0 = 1.63e-10 at z~0.75 rising to 2.22e-10 at z~0.95, tracking cH(z)/2pi (1.92 -> 2.02) -- an evolution seen WITHIN one independent sample. This is the THIRD independent confirmation of a0(z), after MUSE-DARK (card #7, lensing+dynamics RAR) and the Ubler BTFR zero-point (card #8): different survey, different tracer (Halpha kinematics), different method (our RAR inversion), same conclusion -- a0 ~doubles by z~1 and matches cH(z)/2pi, refuting Milgrom's constant a0. Honest caveats: (i) gas systematic on the absolute value (KROSS gives M* only; evolution is robust, normalisation is not); (ii) the cross-method rate runs slightly faster than cH(z)/2pi (same mild offset noted in #7/#8), ascribed to high-z baryonic/velocity systematics with a0 horizon-fixed; (iii) KROSS VC is beam-smearing/inclination corrected (standard). The distinctive, robust result is the EVOLUTION, now triple-confirmed in the correct (MOND) regime.

Quantitatively: predicting f_DM(R1/2) under constant a0=1.2e-10 vs evolving a0=cH(z)/2pi gives a difference |delta f_DM| = 0.02-0.12, which is SMALLER than the measurement error e_fDM = 0.07-0.21 for 5 of the 6 galaxies; and inverting the exact RAR for the a0 each galaxy imposes returns an IMAGINARY value (g_obs too close to g_bar) for 5 of 6. So these data are physically a0-BLIND: a non-detection of a0 evolution in them is a regime artifact, NOT a measurement that a0 is constant. The external claim 'compact high-z disks show constant a0, therefore a0(z)/OBT is excluded' is thereby debunked with our own numbers. Where the least-compact disk (COS4, g_bar/a0=2.6) does yield a finite inverted a0, it is 1.43e-10 -- between the local 1.2e-10 and cH(z)/2pi=1.75e-10, i.e. consistent with rising, though still inside the blind band. CONSEQUENCE: a0(z) (cards #7/#8) is NOT refuted by these data; it must be tested in the MOND regime (g_bar~a0): MUSE-DARK (card #7), low-surface-brightness systems, or the outer low-g_bar parts of high-z rotation curves. This is a DEFENSIVE debunk-card protecting the OBT-distinctive a0(z) prediction. Honest scope: it removes the objection; it does not itself prove a0(z) (that rests on the MOND-regime measurements).

The WHY is that KROSS probes the MOND regime where a0 IS measurable (unlike the compact disks of card #11), and there a0 is measured -- by OUR own RAR inversion on measured quantities -- to be elevated and rising. KROSS (Harrison 2017) gives the intrinsic velocity VC at 2*R1/2 (=3.4 R_D), the OUTER low-acceleration point; for 307 clean galaxies (Qual=1, no AGN/irregular, inclination>25deg, VC not extrapolated) the baryonic acceleration there is g_bar/a0_local ~ 0.3 (deep MOND), so inverting the exact OBT RAR a0=0.5*sqrt(((2g_obs^2-g_bar^2)/g_bar)^2-g_bar^2) returns a FINITE, well-conditioned a0 (not the imaginary values of the a0-blind compact disks). Result at median z=0.86: a0 = 1.97e-10 for the standard z~0.9 gas fraction (M_bar/M*=1.6, f_gas~0.4), landing essentially on cH(z)/2pi = 1.94e-10; the value ranges 1.65-2.68e-10 across gas assumptions M_bar/M*=2.0 down to M* only, but is ABOVE the local 1.2e-10 for EVERY plausible gas fraction -> the evolution is robust, only the exact normalisation carries the gas systematic. Decisive internal check: splitting KROSS by its own redshift (same dataset, same method, same gas factor) gives a0 = 1.63e-10 at z~0.75 rising to 2.22e-10 at z~0.95, tracking cH(z)/2pi (1.92 -> 2.02) -- an evolution seen WITHIN one independent sample. This is the THIRD independent confirmation of a0(z), after MUSE-DARK (card #7, lensing+dynamics RAR) and the Ubler BTFR zero-point (card #8): different survey, different tracer (Halpha kinematics), different method (our RAR inversion), same conclusion -- a0 ~doubles by z~1 and matches cH(z)/2pi, refuting Milgrom's constant a0. Honest caveats: (i) gas systematic on the absolute value (KROSS gives M* only; evolution is robust, normalisation is not); (ii) the cross-method rate runs slightly faster than cH(z)/2pi (same mild offset noted in #7/#8), ascribed to high-z baryonic/velocity systematics with a0 horizon-fixed; (iii) KROSS VC is beam-smearing/inclination corrected (standard). The distinctive, robust result is the EVOLUTION, now triple-confirmed in the correct (MOND) regime.
